subject: Retention thresholds and selective redaction workflow for regulated accounts
messages:
From: Emily Hunter <emily.hunter@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Retention and redaction options for PHI/PII — Acme onboarding

Hi Rishi / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo this week. Acme Health is moving toward a pilot and Security asked for a concise Q&A on two items we must nail down before contract signature:

1) Maximum allowed retention windows for PHI-backed datasets (both short-lived tokens and permanent records).
2) Practical options for targeted redaction (field-level vs. full-record) and how that affects auditability and backups.

Specifically: we need to know whether you can configure per-account retention (e.g., 30/90/365 days), whether redaction can be performed at ingestion (before indexing) versus post-processing, and the timeline for complete deletion across hot storage, backups, and KV caches.

Can you send a clear summary, including any limits or caveats we should surface to our legal/regulatory team? We also attached the initial intake matrix.

Best,
Emily
Emily Hunter
Head of Security Programs, Acme Health
(emily.hunter@acmehealth.com)

Attachment: redaction-options-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Subject: Re: Retention and redaction options for PHI/PII — Acme onboarding

Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the matrix. Looping in Vivek (platform/privacy) and Monica (solutions) so we can give a concise, authoritative answer.

Quick clarifying Qs before we respond in detail:
- When you say "permanent records" do you mean records retained indefinitely by Acme (customer-controlled), or records that Redwood would retain for product telemetry/debugging?
- Do you need an option for automated deterministic redaction (strip and store redaction token) versus irreversible deletion?

If you can say which datasets are in-scope for the pilot (PHI transcripts vs. user profile metadata), that will let us indicate the recommended approach.

Will follow up shortly with a short options table and SLA timelines.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Emily Hunter <emily.hunter@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention and redaction options for PHI/PII — Acme onboarding

Emily, Rishi, Monica — thanks for flagging. Below is a concise breakdown of our supported approaches and the operational caveats (keeps it short for legal/security review):

1) Per-account retention windows (recommended)- Configurable retention buckets at the account/route level: 30, 90, 180, 365, or custom (in days).- Enforcement: primary data store + live KV cache eviction are enforced immediately after TTL expiration.- Caveat: backups (snapshot cadence) are retained for the configured backup-retention period — see item #4.

2) Redaction approaches- Ingestion-time field-level redaction: we can apply deterministic masking or hashing (pseudonymization) on configured fields before they are stored. This preserves auditability because original values are never written to primary stores.- Post-ingest selective redaction: we can run sweep jobs that redact specified fields retroactively; these are asynchronous and are scheduled with priority options.- Full-record irreversible deletion: removes the entire record from primary stores and KV caches. Irreversible means we do not keep a plaintext copy; however, traces in logs/telemetry may remain per retention policy.

3) Impact on auditability and logs- Audit logs include metadata about redaction, the actor, and timestamps. We can produce redaction reports for the specified time range.- If ingestion-time redaction is used, auditors will see hashes/pseudonyms (not original PHI). We can provide a mapping file to Acme under an encrypted key-holder process if you require reversible pseudonymization (requires explicit contractual and KMS controls).

4) Backups and deletion timeline- Primary store deletion: within 24 hours of the deletion request or TTL expiration (typical).- KV cache eviction: immediate to 2 hours depending on cache pressure.- Snapshots/backups: our scheduled snapshots occur daily; snapshots are overwritten/eligible for purge after the configured backup-retention window. For a strict 30-day retention, backups containing the data may persist for up to 30 days beyond deletion request.- Crash-consistency / immutable snapshots: in air-gapped/private deployments we can shorten snapshot retention by agreement (often subject to SRE windowing).

5) Deletion SLA & proof- We support an Erasure API that returns a job ID and completion timestamp. For enterprise contracts we can commit to a 72-hour full-erasure SLA from job completion to removal from all searchable stores and KV caches (excludes backup windows unless contracted).

6) Recommended patterns for regulated clients- Ingest-and-redact (preferred): redact PII/PHI at ingestion, store pseudonyms, and retain mapping only under customer‑controlled KMS for reversible lookups.- Ephemeral routing for PHI processing: if you need sub-30-day retention, route those requests to a dedicated ephemeral tenant with shorter snapshot windows.

Next steps: Monica — I'll hand this to you to translate into a short one‑page summary for Acme's legal/security. I can attach a sample Erasure API response and our redaction matrix.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Platform & Privacy, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Hunter <emily.hunter@acmehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T12:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention and redaction options for PHI/PII — Acme onboarding

Thanks Vivek — that's very helpful. A couple of follow ups so we can finalize an internal brief:

• For the Erasure API job ID: will the job include a cryptographic proof (hash) that the deletion covered the specified object IDs? Our auditors prefer a verifiable fingerprint.
• For backups: if we select a 30-day primary retention, can we contractually cap backup retention to 7 days for the pilot environment only?
• For reversible pseudonymization: describe the KMS model you support (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed). We need BYOK for the pilot.

If you can send a one-page attestation for the deletion timeline and a sample Erasure API response, we can move to signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Emily
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Hunter <emily.hunter@acmehealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28T14:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention and redaction options for PHI/PII — Acme onboarding

Emily — great questions. Short answers and attached artifacts.

• Erasure API proof: yes — the job response includes before/after object-ID digests (SHA-256) and a job completion signature we can sign with our intermediate key. We can provide the sample JSON payload (attached).
• Backup cap for pilot: for Hosted Enterprise customers we can offer a pilot amendment to cap backup retention to 7 days for the pilot tenant only; this requires a short SOW and operational runbook to ensure snapshot cadence is adjusted (we've done this previously for customers in clinical trials).
• KMS model: we support BYOK (customer KMS) for reversible pseudonym mapping and for encryption-at-rest keys. Redwood-managed keys are the default, but BYOK is available for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: redwood-residency-summary.pdf (summary of retention & deletion behaviors), sample-erasure-api-response.json (stub).

Next steps: I'll convert Vivek's breakdown into a one-page attestation and drop the artifacts into the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redaction-guidance). Rishi — I'll need you to confirm the pilot SOW language for backup cap.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
